title: STIX and TAXII
summary: STIX is a structured language for expressing cyber threat intelligence and TAXII is the transport protocol that moves it between organisations, and together they are the standards that make machine-to-machine sharing practical. STIX is a graph-based data model, serialised as JSON, whose objects fall into domain objects, cyber observable objects and relationship objects. Domain objects describe high-level intelligence such as threat actors, campaigns, intrusion sets, malware, attack patterns, indicators, reports, courses of action and identities. Cyber observable objects describe the technical artefacts an analyst records, including files, processes, network traffic, domain names and registry keys. Relationship objects connect them, so an indicator can reference an attack pattern and a report can bundle the whole product. Patterning gives indicators a precise, testable expression language, which is what allows a detection platform to consume them without hand translation. TAXII is the transport layer: a client polls or subscribes to a server, and the server exposes API roots containing collections of STIX objects. TAXII collections are browsable sets of objects, while channels support publish and subscribe exchange. Versioning and identifier discipline matter operationally. Every object carries a stable identifier and a modified timestamp, and consumers deduplicate and resolve updates on that basis, so sloppy identifier generation causes silent divergence between sharing partners. Real deployments also need trust decisions, because receiving a bundle is receiving attacker-influenced content. Analysts must honour handling markings that express sharing caveats, and they must decide what tooling does when an object is malformed or uses extensions the consumer does not implement. A working pipeline therefore combines schema validation, deduplication, enrichment, confidence handling and a documented policy for what is automatically blocked, what is only hunted, and what is discarded.
objectives: You will be able to distinguish STIX domain objects, cyber observable objects and relationship objects and explain what each is for.
You will be able to validate, deduplicate and update STIX objects using identifiers and modified timestamps.
You will be able to explain how TAXII collections differ from channels and which fits a given sharing requirement.
You will be able to apply handling markings and confidence information when a bundle arrives from a partner.
You will be able to describe the failure modes of an unvalidated feed and the controls that prevent them.
You will be able to write a consumption policy that separates objects to block, to hunt and to discard.
